title: 集成 V0.1 Alpha 候选并执行 release gate
risks: V0.1 Alpha remains blocked by 15 non-passed capabilities, six blocked release targets and the V01-008 partial input; completing V01-009 does not authorize release.
Production authentication, PostgreSQL runtime composition, business APIs, TLS/secrets, metadata, exact deduplication and product-level backup/restore are not implemented or integrated.
Production physical writes remain disabled; the V01-007 task-owned sandbox is not production durability evidence and M0-006-G2 remains open.
Windows SCM, Docker daemon, Linux systemd/root and release-like large-file evidence require approved external environments and remain unexecuted here.
The current Windows runner cannot execute the Ubuntu-only 500k profile or create symlinks under the non-elevated token; PostgreSQL integration also lacks its dedicated local environment.

architecture_review.module: Repository-only V0.1 Alpha release integration and evidence gate
reused_existing_logic: tests/architecture/m0-gates.json and check_release_gates.py remain the only release-target allow/deny algorithm; V01-009 invokes the checker in bounded isolated subprocesses.
Existing task registry and handoff results provide task state, while eng/server-release-policy.json provides the V01-008 host readiness flags.
Existing fast-merge and scheduled-release workflows plus ci-tiers.json are extended without creating a parallel CI tier.
V01-001 through V01-008 public handoff evidence is read without reaching into module Infrastructure or business tables.
duplicated_logic: Capability identifiers, expected current classifications and evidence paths are intentionally pinned in the validator as a fail-closed anti-forgery contract; release-target decisions themselves are not duplicated.
Path containment and reparse checks are repeated at repository-evidence and output-write trust boundaries because each boundary accepts different inputs.
cross_module_access: The implementation lives only in repository/release tooling and reads source-controlled policies and public handoffs; it adds no product runtime reference.
No service, app, provider, gateway, integration, migration, generated SDK or shared wire contract implementation changed.
Production file writes, authentication bypasses, anonymous business APIs and alternate databases remain absent and fail closed.
All optional report writes are confined to the V01-009 runtime sandbox and never inspect asset contents.
contract_changes: Adds the internal repository release-audit policy contract v01-009/1; it does not change a product wire or database contract.
Fast-merge now audits policy consistency, while the manual scheduled release job requires the aggregate readiness decision.
architecture_tests: 13 Alpha validator tests cover mutation, task/status drift, gate failure, timeout, duplicate JSON keys, evidence containment, output ownership and Windows path aliases.
5 repository tests bind the machine policy to fast-merge, scheduled-release, open M0 gates, host fail-closed flags and readiness documentation.
Final repository verifier passed with 14 architecture tests and the existing handoff, migration, SDK, Web and source policies.
Affected full verification includes 185 .NET, 54 repository, 32 release Python, 39 local database, 14 SDK Python, 21 AssetLink and 6 Chromium tests plus TypeScript and Kotlin SDK builds.
v0.1-start returned 0; v0.1-release and aggregate --require-ready each returned the expected 3.
technical_debt: Implement production authentication, database runtime and read-only business host composition as separate owner-scoped tasks before claiming an end-to-end Alpha.
Complete TLS/secrets, metadata, exact deduplication and product-level backup/restore with their own contracts and evidence.
Keep production writes disabled until the durable adapter, database journal, audit, conflict, capacity, strong-hash and trash evidence closes M0-006-G2.
Run and independently review the large-file, Windows SCM, Docker daemon and Linux systemd/root gates in approved isolated environments, then formally adjudicate V01-008.
Run the PostgreSQL 16.15 and Ubuntu 500k scheduled profiles in their declared CI environments before any release candidate decision.
